correctness.rationale: The construction is an exact infinite-dimensional diagonal calculation. The full g-frame sum equals sum_k (1+2 epsilon_k+1/15)|x_k|^2, while the scaled sum is exactly (1/3)||x||^2. Each scaling block is positive and bounded, but its norm is 2^j, so the direct-sum block operator is unbounded. No finite experiment is used.

evidence: A close published result shows that an unbounded scalar diagonal multiplier may preserve a K-frame through a bounded composition on the analysis range.
That result uses scalar K-frame coefficients and does not satisfy the present hypothesis that every g-frame analysis block is bounded below with liminf operator norm positive.
The present example instead uses invertible operator-valued blocks and isolates the norm-versus-minimum-modulus error in the two published scalability statements.

value.rationale: The bounded-block assertion is used to turn local diagonal scalings into a globally bounded preconditioner and is repeated from the 2021 g-frame theory into the 2024 K-g-frame extension. The counterexample shows that the claimed necessity fails even when every analysis block is positive, diagonal, and invertible, while the scaled family is exactly tight. It also identifies the mathematically relevant replacement: control of the scaling on the analysis range.
